questions.q: Why would you package content into an app instead of just sharing individual reports?
options: An app bundles a whole collection of dashboards, reports, and semantic models into one clean, navigable package for a broad audience
Apps are required before any report can be viewed at all
Apps remove the need for any Power BI license
Apps and individual report sharing are functionally identical
questions.explain: Sharing individual reports works for one or two people, but a whole department needing a collection of content is better served by one packaged, read-only app than many separate share links.

questions.q: What is the correct order of tabs when publishing an app?
options: Setup, then Content, then Audience
Audience, then Setup, then Content
Content, then Audience, then Setup
There is only one tab, with everything on it at once
questions.explain: Setup captures the app's name/description/theme, Content is where you add the workspace's reports/dashboards, and Audience is where you define who sees what.

questions.q: What does creating multiple audiences in an app let you do?
options: Show or hide different content, and grant different share/build permissions, to different groups of users within the same app
Nothing — every audience always sees identical content
Create a completely separate app for each audience automatically
Limit the app to only one audience total
questions.explain: Audiences are what make one app flexible for a real organization — a Sales audience and a Leadership audience can see entirely different content from the exact same published app.

questions.q: If content is hidden from an audience's navigation, but a user in that audience has a direct link to it, what happens?
options: They can still open it — hiding controls navigation visibility, not actual security
The direct link is automatically blocked
They are removed from the app entirely
The content becomes permanently inaccessible to everyone
questions.explain: Just like with report sharing, hiding content from an app audience's navigation is a clutter-reduction choice, not a security boundary — a direct link still works.

questions.q: When you update an already-published app, what happens to newly added content by default?
options: It's marked invisible to existing audiences until you manually unhide it in each audience group
It's automatically visible to every existing audience immediately
The entire app resets to a blank state
Updating an app is not possible once it's published
questions.explain: New content added during an update starts hidden for every audience — you have to go into each audience group and manually make it visible, unlike the very first publish.
